plugins.name: synergy
plugins.description: Development workflow plugin for GitHub story work and for work that stays on your machine. Say 'start the next story' and it picks an issue from your backlog, plans it, builds it, runs tests, opens a PR, has the PR reviewed independently by agents in a fresh context, and merges it on projects that turn on auto-merge. If Claude Code's auto mode blocks a run from approving or merging its own PR, the run stops cleanly and names the user setting that lets it finish. Selection reads org issue fields (Stage, Priority, Effort, Ownership) and the area, feature and story tree, never labels or board cards; every issue sits under a permanent area epic, which is never picked or closed, and a scheduled board-sync keeps every issue's Stage in step. Dependencies decide order, not eligibility: a blocker inherits the priority of what waits on it, execute builds a named story's prerequisites first, and bulk-execute fills an effort budget with stories one Priority step apart, linked or not, as at most two pull requests built one after the other, in waves, and wf schedules and integrates the independent ones it builds in parallel. Filing an issue sets its Classification areas, and the wf CLI reads and writes issues in as few GitHub requests as it can: starting a build, opening the PR, blocking a story and cleaning up at exit are each one command that prints a one-line result when everything lands, and a run that already passed preflight skips the preflight skill. For local work, 'build this' plans, builds, verifies and commits with no issue or PR, pr-review reviews a local change as well as a PR, verify-feature writes the report a person reads before merging, in the chat only, spec-hardening tests a spec against the codebase before it is built, in the chat only, and release-notes writes user and internal release notes, grouped under each issue's area epic, which execute and bulk-execute record on each story when it reaches Done. It posts only to GitHub: anything that would post to Azure DevOps, GitLab or Bitbucket asks first, each session is told which platform hosts the repository, and a personal allowlist on each machine blocks GitHub writes outside the orgs and account it names. One grill skill runs every interview. Keeps what loads into each session small.
